domain: CoreMotion and all motion/inertial sensing on iOS 26 / iOS 27 beta (July 2026) — personal sideloaded quantified-self app, hardware = iPhone + Apple Watch + AirPods + iPad

capabilities.stream: Timestamp on EVERY motion sample (accelerometer, gyro, magnetometer, deviceMotion, HF heart rate, recorded data)
capabilities.api: CMLogItem.timestamp (var timestamp: TimeInterval)
capabilities.permission: none (inherited on objects that themselves need NSMotionUsageDescription)
capabilities.resolution: Seconds since DEVICE BOOT — not wall-clock, not Unix epoch
capabilities.notes: Apple: 'The timestamp is the amount of time in seconds since the device booted.' To get wall-clock: Date(timeIntervalSinceNow: timestamp - ProcessInfo.processInfo.systemUptime). The boot offset changes after every reboot, so a long-running logger MUST persist the offset per session or all historical samples silently shift. This is the most common data-integrity bug in QS motion logging.

capabilities.stream: Step count
capabilities.api: CMPedometerData.numberOfSteps (NSNumber, non-optional); CMPedometer.isStepCountingAvailable()
capabilities.permission: NSMotionUsageDescription (Info.plist) + runtime 'Motion & Fitness' prompt; CMPedometer.authorizationStatus() -> CMAuthorizationStatus {.notDetermined,.restricted,.denied,.authorized}
capabilities.resolution: Live updates via startUpdates(from:withHandler:) — cumulative since the start date, delivered on a serial dispatch queue as new data arrives
capabilities.notes: Apple, queryPedometerData(from:to:withHandler:): 'Only the past seven days worth of data is stored and available for you to retrieve.' Apple, startUpdates: 'When the app is suspended, the delivery of updates stops temporarily. Upon returning to foreground or background execution, the pedometer object begins updates again.' Battery: near-zero — the motion coprocessor counts steps whether or not your app runs; you are reading a cache.

capabilities.stream: Distance travelled on foot
capabilities.api: CMPedometerData.distance (NSNumber?, meters); CMPedometer.isDistanceAvailable()
capabilities.notes: 'This value reflects the distance traveled while walking and running.' nil if distance estimation is unsupported on the device.

capabilities.stream: Floors ascended
capabilities.api: CMPedometerData.floorsAscended (NSNumber?); CMPedometer.isFloorCountingAvailable()
capabilities.resolution: Integer floors; Apple defines 'a single floor has a height of approximately three meters'
capabilities.notes: Requires a barometer (iPhone 6 and later). Counts only stairs walked — 'does not reflect the floors ascended by elevator or other assisted means'. nil on devices without floor counting.

capabilities.stream: Floors descended
capabilities.api: CMPedometerData.floorsDescended (NSNumber?)
capabilities.notes: Same barometer requirement and elevator exclusion as floorsAscended.

capabilities.stream: Instantaneous pace (seconds per meter)
capabilities.api: CMPedometerData.currentPace (NSNumber?); CMPedometer.isPaceAvailable()
capabilities.notes: HARD LIMIT: 'The value in this property is nil when you are performing a query for historical pedometer data.' currentPace and currentCadence exist ONLY on live startUpdates deliveries; the 7-day backfill never contains them. If you want pace history you must be running live.

capabilities.stream: Cadence (steps per second)
capabilities.api: CMPedometerData.currentCadence (NSNumber?); CMPedometer.isCadenceAvailable()
capabilities.notes: Same live-only restriction as currentPace: nil on all historical queries.

capabilities.stream: Average active pace over an interval
capabilities.api: CMPedometerData.averageActivePace (NSNumber?)
capabilities.backfill: 7 days — this one DOES survive a historical query
capabilities.notes: The exception to the pace rule: 'When you perform historical queries, the property is set to the average active pace between startDate and endDate.' Averages only periods of activity, omitting inactivity. nil if the user didn't move in the window.

capabilities.stream: Walking start/stop events (pedestrian activity pause/resume)
capabilities.api: CMPedometer.startEventUpdates(handler:) -> CMPedometerEvent {date: Date; type: CMPedometerEventType .pause / .resume}; CMPedometer.isPedometerEventTrackingAvailable(); stopEventUpdates()
capabilities.backfill: none — no historical query exists for events
capabilities.notes: There is NO queryPedometerEvents API. Events are live-stream only, so they are lost while suspended. Gives you precise walk-bout boundaries you cannot reconstruct from queryPedometerData.

capabilities.stream: Motion activity classification: stationary / walking / running / automotive / cycling / unknown, each with confidence
capabilities.api: CMMotionActivityManager.startActivityUpdates(to:withHandler:) and queryActivityStarting(from:to:to:withHandler:) -> CMMotionActivity {stationary, walking, running, automotive, cycling, unknown : Bool; startDate: Date; confidence: CMMotionActivityConfidence .low/.medium/.high}; isActivityAvailable(); stopActivityUpdates()
capabilities.resolution: Event-driven — the handler fires only when the classification CHANGES. Apple: 'A delay of up to several minutes in reported activities is expected.'
capabilities.notes: Flags are NOT mutually exclusive — Apple's own example: a car stopped at a red light sets automotive AND stationary true. All six can be false simultaneously. Apple, startActivityUpdates: 'updates are not delivered while your app is suspended. If updates arrived while your app was suspended, the last update is delivered when it resumes. To get ALL of the updates that occurred while your app was suspended, use queryActivityStarting'. An empty range returns error CMErrorUnknown, not an empty array.

capabilities.stream: Raw accelerometer (x, y, z in g)
capabilities.api: CMMotionManager.startAccelerometerUpdates(to:withHandler:) / startAccelerometerUpdates() + .accelerometerData -> CMAccelerometerData.acceleration: CMAcceleration{x,y,z}; accelerometerUpdateInterval; isAccelerometerAvailable / isAccelerometerActive; stopAccelerometerUpdates()
capabilities.permission: none at runtime — NO prompt for raw sensors on iPhone/iPad. (Include NSMotionUsageDescription anyway; the moment any other CoreMotion class runs it becomes mandatory.)
capabilities.resolution: Apple: 'The maximum frequency at which you can request updates is hardware-dependent but is usually at least 100 Hz.' Requesting higher silently clamps to the hardware max. Units: 1.0 = 9.8 m/s².
capabilities.notes: THE key asymmetry: raw accelerometer/gyro/magnetometer/deviceMotion require NO user permission prompt at all, while step counts do. Background: there is no CoreMotion background mode (see blockers); you must already be running in background for another reason (UIBackgroundModes 'location' with CLLocationManager.allowsBackgroundLocationUpdates = true, or 'audio'). Battery: HIGH and continuous — Apple: 'The device-motion service captures motion data using special hardware, and running this hardware consumes additional power.'

capabilities.stream: Raw gyroscope (rotation rate x, y, z in rad/s)
capabilities.api: CMMotionManager.startGyroUpdates(to:withHandler:) / startGyroUpdates() + .gyroData -> CMGyroData.rotationRate: CMRotationRate{x,y,z}; gyroUpdateInterval; isGyroAvailable / isGyroActive; stopGyroUpdates()
capabilities.notes: Raw = biased. The bias-corrected version is CMDeviceMotion.rotationRate. Apple: 'The value of this property contains a measurement of gyroscope data whose bias has been removed... The identically named property of CMGyroData gives the raw data from the gyroscope.'

capabilities.stream: Raw magnetometer (magnetic field x, y, z in microteslas, device bias INCLUDED)
capabilities.api: CMMotionManager.startMagnetometerUpdates(to:withHandler:) / startMagnetometerUpdates() + .magnetometerData -> CMMagnetometerData.magneticField: CMMagneticField{x,y,z}; magnetometerUpdateInterval; isMagnetometerAvailable / isMagnetometerActive; stopMagnetometerUpdates()
capabilities.notes: Raw values include the device's own magnetic bias. For a bias-removed field use CMDeviceMotion.magneticField. Useful QS signal: raw magnetometer variance is a strong proxy for indoor/outdoor transitions and proximity to vehicles/electronics.

capabilities.stream: Device attitude — orientation as roll/pitch/yaw (radians), rotation matrix, and quaternion
capabilities.api: CMDeviceMotion.attitude -> CMAttitude {roll, pitch, yaw: Double; rotationMatrix: CMRotationMatrix (m11..m33); quaternion: CMQuaternion (x,y,z,w); multiply(byInverseOf:)}. Started via CMMotionManager.startDeviceMotionUpdates(using:to:withHandler:) / (to:withHandler:) / (using:) / ()
capabilities.resolution: deviceMotionUpdateInterval; usually up to ~100 Hz (Apple's own sample uses 1/60 s)
capabilities.notes: Reference frame chosen at start: CMAttitudeReferenceFrame.xArbitraryZVertical (default), .xArbitraryCorrectedZVertical, .xMagneticNorthZVertical, .xTrueNorthZVertical. Check availableAttitudeReferenceFrames() first. North-referenced frames run the magnetometer and cost more battery. multiply(byInverseOf:) gives delta-attitude, which is what you want for gesture/posture work.

capabilities.stream: Bias-corrected rotation rate (fused gyro)
capabilities.api: CMDeviceMotion.rotationRate -> CMRotationRate{x,y,z} rad/s
capabilities.notes: Prefer this over CMGyroData.rotationRate for anything analytic — gyro bias drifts with temperature and would otherwise integrate into fake rotation.

capabilities.stream: Gravity vector (direction of down, in device frame)
capabilities.api: CMDeviceMotion.gravity -> CMAcceleration{x,y,z}
capabilities.notes: total acceleration = gravity + userAcceleration. Gravity alone is the cheapest reliable 'phone flat on a table / in a pocket / held up' classifier.

capabilities.stream: User acceleration (gravity removed — the acceleration the person imparts)
capabilities.api: CMDeviceMotion.userAcceleration -> CMAcceleration{x,y,z}
capabilities.notes: The single highest-value raw stream for a QS app: it is what step/gesture/tremor/vehicle-motion classifiers are built on, and it needs no permission prompt.

capabilities.stream: Calibrated magnetic field + calibration accuracy
capabilities.api: CMDeviceMotion.magneticField -> CMCalibratedMagneticField {field: CMMagneticField; accuracy: CMMagneticFieldCalibrationAccuracy .uncalibrated/.low/.medium/.high}
capabilities.notes: 'the total magnetic field in the device's vicinity WITHOUT device bias' = earth field + surrounding fields − device bias. If no magnetometer, accuracy == .uncalibrated. CMMotionManager.showsDeviceMovementDisplay (Bool) controls whether iOS may show the figure-8 calibration HUD.

capabilities.stream: Compass heading (degrees relative to the chosen reference frame)
capabilities.api: CMDeviceMotion.heading -> Double (0.0–360.0)
capabilities.permission: none at runtime for the value itself; TRUE north additionally requires CoreLocation authorization (NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription)
capabilities.notes: 'This value is available only when the frame of reference is xMagneticNorthZVertical or xTrueNorthZVertical. If the reference frame is xArbitraryZVertical or xArbitraryCorrectedZVertical, this property contains a NEGATIVE number to indicate the heading is invalid.' xTrueNorthZVertical yields CMErrorTrueNorthNotAvailable when device location isn't yet known — i.e. true north is a location-gated derivative of a motion API.

capabilities.stream: Heading accuracy estimate (NEW in iOS 27)
capabilities.api: CMDeviceMotion.headingAccuracy -> Double
capabilities.notes: Marked BETA on iOS/iPadOS/Mac Catalyst/visionOS/watchOS 27.0 in Apple's own documentation data; already shipping on macOS 10.15. Apple has published NO abstract or discussion. Units undocumented (presumably degrees, one-sigma, matching CLHeading.headingAccuracy convention) — verify empirically before trusting.

capabilities.stream: Which physical sensor produced this device-motion sample (phone vs left/right AirPod)
capabilities.api: CMDeviceMotion.sensorLocation -> CMDeviceMotion.SensorLocation {.default, .headphoneLeft, .headphoneRight}
capabilities.permission: none at runtime (NSMotionUsageDescription required when the source is CMHeadphoneMotionManager)
capabilities.notes: Non-obvious side channel: with AirPods this tells you WHICH earbud is the active motion source. It flips when the user removes one bud, giving a de-facto single-bud-worn signal without any dedicated API.

capabilities.stream: Relative altitude change + raw barometric pressure
capabilities.api: CMAltimeter.startRelativeAltitudeUpdates(to:withHandler:) -> CMAltitudeData {relativeAltitude: NSNumber (meters, 0 for first sample); pressure: NSNumber (kPa)}; isRelativeAltitudeAvailable(); stopRelativeAltitudeUpdates()
capabilities.permission: NSMotionUsageDescription + Motion & Fitness runtime prompt; CMAltimeter.authorizationStatus()
capabilities.resolution: Apple: 'Core Motion generates events at regular intervals (regardless of whether the data has changed)' — empirically ~1 Hz. Sub-10 cm altitude sensitivity.
capabilities.notes: Requires a barometer (iPhone 6+). relativeAltitude is zeroed at the first event of each session, so it is useless across app restarts — but the raw `pressure` field is absolute kPa and IS comparable across sessions. Log pressure, derive altitude yourself. Very low power relative to the IMU.

capabilities.stream: Absolute altitude above sea level (+ accuracy, + precision)
capabilities.api: CMAltimeter.startAbsoluteAltitudeUpdates(to:withHandler:) -> CMAbsoluteAltitudeData {altitude: Double (m MSL, can be negative); accuracy: Double (1-sigma uncertainty, m); precision: Double (recommended display resolution, m)}; isAbsoluteAltitudeAvailable(); stopAbsoluteAltitudeUpdates()
capabilities.permission: NSMotionUsageDescription (the ONLY key Apple documents); location authorization empirically also implicated — CONTESTED, see notes
capabilities.notes: HARDWARE GATE: 'Absolute altitude is only available on iPhone 12 and later and Apple Watch 6 or SE and later.' CONTESTED: Apple names only NSMotionUsageDescription, but this is barometer+GNSS fusion. Apple forum thread 751610 (iOS 17.4.1+) reports the value collapsing to exactly the GPS altitude — 'The accelerometer data does not seem to be taken into account anymore' — and a reply speculates Apple 'linked startAbsoluteAltitudeUpdates totally to a location data' such that a coarse CLLocationManager distanceFilter/accuracy degrades it. No Apple engineer replied. Same thread reports devices becoming persistently uncalibrated after long indoor periods ('my watch never re-calibrated'). Treat location authorization as a practical prerequisite and validate accuracy on-device.

capabilities.stream: Recorded raw accelerometer history — 50 Hz, captured while your app is suspended OR TERMINATED
capabilities.api: CMSensorRecorder.recordAccelerometer(forDuration:) then accelerometerData(from:to:) -> CMSensorDataList (enumerable) of CMRecordedAccelerometerData {acceleration: CMAcceleration; startDate: Date; identifier: UInt64 batch id}; isAccelerometerRecordingAvailable(); authorizationStatus()
capabilities.permission: NSMotionUsageDescription + Motion & Fitness runtime prompt. NOTE: calling recordAccelerometer(forDuration:) is itself what triggers the prompt and creates the Settings toggle — there is no requestAuthorization method.
capabilities.resolution: Fixed 50 Hz. Single record call ≤ 43,200 s (12 h). Single query span must be ≤ 12 h.
capabilities.notes: NOT DEPRECATED as of iOS 26 / iOS 27 beta — I checked every platform availability flag on the class and all its methods; only isAuthorizedForRecording() carries a deprecation (iOS 11 / watchOS 4, superseded by authorizationStatus()). The class still sits under 'Accelerometers' in the current framework index. Apple: 'The system records the data for the specified amount of time, EVEN IF YOUR APP IS SUSPENDED OR TERMINATED. The collected data remains accessible to your app for up to three days... There may be a delay of up to three minutes before new samples are available.' CONTESTED BEHAVIOR: forum threads 15470 and 113845 report accelerometerData(from:to:) returning nil indefinitely on iPhone; counter-reports attribute it to (a) not yet authorized, (b) the ≤3-minute delivery lag, (c) hardware gating — isAccelerometerRecordingAvailable() reported true on iPhone XR but false on iPhone SE / 6s Plus, i.e. A10+ only, a gate Apple has never documented. Battery: large power impact per Apple guidance and forum consensus. VERIFY ON YOUR OWN DEVICE FIRST — this is simultaneously the highest-value API in the domain for a free-tier app and the one most likely to disappoint.

capabilities.stream: Recorded device-motion history (NEW in iOS 27 — fused attitude/gravity/userAcceleration with batch identity)
capabilities.api: CMRecordedDeviceMotion : CMDeviceMotion {identifier: UInt64; startDate: Date}
capabilities.resolution: unknown — Apple has published no abstract, no discussion, and no producing API
capabilities.notes: MOST INTERESTING iOS 27 FINDING. Structurally the exact analogue of CMRecordedAccelerometerData : CMAccelerometerData (same two added members, same identifier/startDate pair), which strongly implies CMSensorRecorder is gaining a device-motion recording path — offline recall of FUSED motion, not just raw accel. Confirmed via Apple's own doc data: beta on iOS/iPadOS/MacCatalyst/macOS/visionOS/watchOS 27.0, inheritsFrom CMDeviceMotion. No public method in CoreMotion currently returns it, and Apple's Core Motion 'updates' page has no entry newer than September 2024. Track it across the iOS 27 betas.

capabilities.stream: deviceMotionBody — attach an identifiable reference body to device motion (NEW in iOS 27, undocumented)
capabilities.api: CMMotionManager.deviceMotionBody: (any CMBodyIdentifiable)? { get set }; protocol CMBodyIdentifiable : NSObjectProtocol
capabilities.notes: Both symbols exist in Apple's iOS 27 doc data with NO abstract, NO discussion, and NO conforming types published; CMBodyIdentifiable has zero documented members. A settable body on CMMotionManager suggests attitude can be expressed relative to a moving reference body (vehicle/vessel/treadmill frame) rather than only the Earth frames of CMAttitudeReferenceFrame. Speculative — verify against the iOS 27 SDK headers before designing around it.

capabilities.stream: AirPods head orientation — attitude, rotationRate, gravity, userAcceleration, magneticField, sensorLocation (L/R)
capabilities.api: CMHeadphoneMotionManager.startDeviceMotionUpdates(to:withHandler:) / startDeviceMotionUpdates() + .deviceMotion -> CMDeviceMotion?; isDeviceMotionAvailable; isDeviceMotionActive; authorizationStatus(); stopDeviceMotionUpdates()
capabilities.permission: NSMotionUsageDescription — Apple: 'In iOS and macOS, include the NSMotionUsageDescription key... If this key is absent, the system CRASHES your app when you start device-motion updates.' Plus the runtime Motion & Fitness prompt.
capabilities.entitlement: none — see blockers regarding the head-pose entitlement red herring
capabilities.resolution: ~25 Hz — EMPIRICALLY REPORTED by developers, NOT documented by Apple. There is no updateInterval property on CMHeadphoneMotionManager at all; you take what you're given.
capabilities.notes: Requires H1/H2-class AirPods (AirPods Pro, AirPods 3/4, AirPods Max, Beats Fit Pro). Backgrounding: no supported mechanism — no CoreMotion background mode exists, and unlike CMMotionManager there is no documented location/audio piggyback. Community advice to 'enable the Motion & Fitness background mode' (forum thread 715100) is WRONG — no such UIBackgroundMode exists. Since watchOS 11 / iOS 18 the class also supports AirPods motion sourced from Apple Watch (Core Motion updates, June 2024).

capabilities.stream: AirPods connect / disconnect events (delegate)
capabilities.api: CMHeadphoneMotionManagerDelegate.headphoneMotionManagerDidConnect(_:) / headphoneMotionManagerDidDisconnect(_:); CMHeadphoneMotionManager.startConnectionStatusUpdates() / stopConnectionStatusUpdates(); isConnectionStatusActive; delegate
capabilities.minIOS: 14.0 (connect/disconnect monitoring OUTSIDE a motion session added June 2024 / iOS 18 per Core Motion updates)
capabilities.notes: DIRECT ANSWER to 'does this reveal AirPods worn/removed': NO, not as a documented signal. The delegate exposes CONNECTION state only — the callbacks are literally named DidConnect/DidDisconnect and Apple's abstracts read 'after you connect headphones' / 'after you disconnect headphones'. In-ear detection is NOT surfaced by CoreMotion. Two indirect proxies: (a) CMDeviceMotion.sensorLocation flips between .headphoneLeft/.headphoneRight when a bud is removed; (b) with Automatic Ear Detection on, removing both buds routes audio away and typically ends the motion session, surfacing as a disconnect-like transition. Both are inferences, not APIs.

capabilities.stream: Headphone-derived motion activity (walking/running/etc. classified from AirPods, independent of where the phone is)
capabilities.api: CMHeadphoneActivityManager.startActivityUpdates(to:withHandler:) -> CMMotionActivity via CMHeadphoneActivityManager.ActivityHandler = (CMMotionActivity?, Error?) -> Void; isActivityAvailable; isActivityActive; stopActivityUpdates(); authorizationStatus()
capabilities.permission: NSMotionUsageDescription — 'If this key is absent, trying to start headphone activity updates TERMINATES your app.'
capabilities.resolution: Event-driven on classification change; same CMMotionActivity payload as CMMotionActivityManager
capabilities.backfill: none — no historical query exists (unlike CMMotionActivityManager's 7-day queryActivityStarting)
capabilities.notes: Apple: 'This class provides similar information to CMMotionActivityManager, except the activity information comes from HEADPHONE motion, rather than from device motion.' Genuinely additive for QS: it classifies the PERSON even when the phone is on a desk or in another room. Badly underused.

capabilities.stream: Headphone connection status (as an activity-manager stream)
capabilities.api: CMHeadphoneActivityManager.startStatusUpdates(to:withHandler:) -> CMHeadphoneActivityManager.Status {.connected, .disconnected} via StatusHandler = (Status, Error?) -> Void; isStatusAvailable; isStatusActive; stopStatusUpdates()
capabilities.notes: Apple: 'If a compatible set of headphones is already connected before you call this method, the handler is called with a status update of connected for the connected headphones' — level-triggered on start, so you get current state without waiting for a transition. Again: connection, not worn.

capabilities.stream: Batched high-rate accelerometer — 800 Hz on Apple Watch
capabilities.api: CMBatchedSensorManager.startAccelerometerUpdates() / startAccelerometerUpdates(handler: ([CMAccelerometerData]?, Error?) -> Void) / accelerometerUpdates() (async sequence, CMBatchedSensorManager.AccelerometerUpdates) + .accelerometerBatch: [CMAccelerometerData]?; accelerometerDataFrequency: Int; isAccelerometerSupported; isAccelerometerActive; authorizationStatus; stopAccelerometerUpdates()
capabilities.minIOS: watchOS 10.0 (the async accelerometerUpdates() surface is watchOS-only in Apple's doc data; third-party bindings annotate the class iOS 17.0 — conflict noted)
capabilities.resolution: 800 Hz accelerometer, delivered as ONE BATCH PER SECOND (not streamed sample-by-sample). Read accelerometerDataFrequency at runtime rather than hardcoding.
capabilities.backfill: none — live only, and only for the duration of a workout
capabilities.notes: Source for 800 Hz: Apple, WWDC23 session 10179 'What's new in Core Motion' — '800 Hz accelerometer and 200 Hz device motion, compared to 100 Hz with the existing CMMotionManager', 'available on Apple Watch Series 8 and Ultra'. That is an Apple statement, not a community measurement. Apple's class documentation is otherwise entirely blank — no abstracts on any member. AVAILABILITY CONFLICT: Apple marks the async accelerometerUpdates()/deviceMotionUpdates() watchOS 10.0 only, while xamarin-macios annotates the whole class iOS (17,0)/MacCatalyst (17,0); treat iOS availability as unverified. Backgrounding via WKBackgroundModes 'workout-processing'. Battery: very high — 800 Hz IMU plus a live workout session.

capabilities.stream: Batched high-rate device motion — 200 Hz on Apple Watch
capabilities.api: CMBatchedSensorManager.startDeviceMotionUpdates() / startDeviceMotionUpdates(handler: ([CMDeviceMotion]?, Error?) -> Void) / deviceMotionUpdates() (CMBatchedSensorManager.DeviceMotionUpdates) + .deviceMotionBatch: [CMDeviceMotion]?; deviceMotionDataFrequency: Int; isDeviceMotionSupported; isDeviceMotionActive; stopDeviceMotionUpdates()
capabilities.resolution: 200 Hz fused device motion, one batch per second
capabilities.notes: Same WWDC23 source, same Apple Watch Series 8 / Ultra gate, same HKWorkoutSession dependency, same blank Apple documentation. Missing workout session surfaces as CMErrorDomain codes (e.g. 109).

capabilities.stream: Water submersion state (submerged / not submerged) — Apple Watch Ultra
capabilities.api: CMWaterSubmersionManagerDelegate.manager(_:didUpdate: CMWaterSubmersionEvent) -> {date: Date; state: CMWaterSubmersionEvent.State .submerged/.notSubmerged/.unknown}; CMWaterSubmersionManager.waterSubmersionAvailable; authorizationStatus; maximumDepth; delegate; manager(_:errorOccurred:)
capabilities.permission: NSMotionUsageDescription — 'If you don't include a usage description string, your app crashes when you try to instantiate a CMWaterSubmersionManager object.'
capabilities.entitlement: REQUIRED — com.apple.developer.submerged-shallow-depth-and-pressure (Xcode capability 'Shallow Depth and Pressure', 6 m max, self-service) OR com.apple.developer.submerged-depth-and-pressure (full 40 m, Apple approval by application). Without one the delegate receives CMErrorNotEntitled and no further data.
capabilities.minIOS: watchOS 9.0 (iOS 16.0 symbols exist, but waterSubmersionAvailable is true only on Apple Watch Ultra — false everywhere else INCLUDING the Simulator)
capabilities.notes: Also needs WKBackgroundModes = ['underwater-depth']. Merely adding that key keeps your app frontmost for 30 minutes after launch and adds it to the autolaunch-on-submersion list; an extended runtime session auto-starts below 1 m and doesn't time out until 10 min unsubmerged or Water Lock is turned off. Apple Watch Series 10 gained the Shallow Depth and Pressure capability (Core Motion updates, September 2024).

capabilities.stream: Dive depth, water pressure, surface air pressure, depth state
capabilities.api: CMWaterSubmersionManagerDelegate.manager(_:didUpdate: CMWaterSubmersionMeasurement) -> {date: Date; depth: Measurement<UnitLength>?; pressure: Measurement<UnitPressure>?; surfacePressure: Measurement<UnitPressure>; submersionState: CMWaterSubmersionMeasurement.DepthState .notSubmerged/.submergedShallow/.submergedDeep/.approachingMaxDepth/.pastMaxDepth/.sensorDepthError/.unknown}
capabilities.resolution: Apple: 'The system sends measurement updates THREE TIMES A SECOND while the watch is submerged. When the watch is on the surface, the system provides updates at a slower rate, and may stop providing updates if the watch isn't moving.'
capabilities.notes: surfacePressure is delivered even when NOT submerged — meaning this API doubles as a second barometer stream on the Watch. .submergedShallow = <1 m, .submergedDeep = ≥1 m.

capabilities.stream: Water temperature + measurement uncertainty
capabilities.api: CMWaterSubmersionManagerDelegate.manager(_:didUpdate: CMWaterTemperature) -> {date: Date; temperature: Measurement<UnitTemperature>; temperatureUncertainty: Measurement<UnitTemperature>}
capabilities.notes: The only ambient-temperature reading Apple exposes to third parties on any device outside SensorKit. Ships with an explicit uncertainty figure, which is unusual for Apple and worth logging alongside the value.

capabilities.stream: Fall detection event + how the user resolved it
capabilities.api: CMFallDetectionManager.requestAuthorization(handler:) + delegate CMFallDetectionDelegate.fallDetectionManager(_:didDetect:completionHandler:) -> CMFallDetectionEvent {date: Date; resolution: CMFallDetectionEvent.UserResolution .confirmed/.dismissed/.rejected/.unresponsive}; CMFallDetectionManager.isAvailable; authorizationStatus; fallDetectionManagerDidChangeAuthorization(_:)
capabilities.permission: NSFallDetectionUsageDescription (Info.plist) — 'If you don't include a usage description string, your app crashes when you call this API.' A separate runtime prompt from Motion & Fitness.
capabilities.entitlement: REQUIRED AND APPLE-APPROVED — com.apple.developer.health.fall-detection ('Fall Detection Notifications'). Apple: 'CMFallDetectionManager requires an entitlement from Apple. To apply for the entitlement, see fall-detection-api.' HARD BLOCKER on a free Apple ID.
capabilities.minIOS: watchOS 7.2 (entitlement itself listed iOS 13.0 / watchOS 6.0); Apple Watch Series 4 and later
capabilities.resolution: Event-driven, real time; the app is woken or launched in the background with a short runtime window and must call the completion handler before it expires
capabilities.backfill: Recent past — 'each time the user launches your app, the system checks to see if a fall event has occurred during the recent past' (window unspecified by Apple)
capabilities.notes: Apple: 'This entitlement allows the app to run in the background WITHOUT requiring any additional capabilities.' Events may be delivered MORE THAN ONCE (e.g. after a crash and relaunch) — dedupe on .date, which Apple guarantees is unique per event. FREE ALTERNATIVE for a personal app: HealthKit's numberOfTimesFallen quantity type needs no special entitlement, but records only falls the user confirmed or that escalated to emergency services (dismissed falls are dropped) and lags the event.

capabilities.stream: Parkinsonian resting tremor — per-minute severity distribution
capabilities.api: CMMovementDisorderManager.monitorKinesias(forDuration:) then queryTremor(from:to:withHandler:) -> [CMTremorResult] {startDate, endDate: Date; percentUnknown, percentNone, percentSlight, percentMild, percentModerate, percentStrong : Float, summing to 1.0}; isAvailable(); authorizationStatus(); version(); lastProcessedDate(); monitorKinesiasExpirationDate()
capabilities.entitlement: REQUIRED AND APPLE-APPROVED — Apple: 'CMMovementDisorderManager requires an entitlement from Apple.' HARD BLOCKER on a free Apple ID.
capabilities.minIOS: watchOS 5.0 (result classes annotated iOS 12.0 but the manager is watchOS-only)
capabilities.resolution: One result object per ONE-MINUTE interval; detects resting tremor in the 3–7 Hz band
capabilities.backfill: 7 days from time of recording; monitorKinesias(forDuration:) max duration is also 7 days and must be renewed BEFORE expiry (repeat calls extend but can never shorten)
capabilities.notes: The watch must be worn on the MOST AFFECTED arm. Beyond the entitlement, Apple imposes contractual UI obligations: a first-launch intro screen stating purpose, data collected, intended use, whether collection happens in background, and how to opt out — plus verbatim required disclosure text, and the app must only collect from users who self-report or are clinically diagnosed. Results arrive in batches; poll lastProcessedDate().

capabilities.stream: Choreiform dyskinesia (levodopa-induced) — per-minute likelihood
capabilities.api: CMMovementDisorderManager.queryDyskineticSymptom(from:to:withHandler:) -> [CMDyskineticSymptomResult] {startDate, endDate: Date; percentUnlikely, percentLikely : Float, summing to 1.0}
capabilities.notes: Same monitorKinesias(forDuration:) subscription model and the same required verbatim disclosure ('This app is monitoring and collecting your choreiform dyskinesia data, only if you self-report or have been clinically diagnosed with choreiform dyskinesias, and indicate within the app that this is true.').

capabilities.stream: Odometer during workouts — speed, slope, max absolute slope, delta distance, delta altitude, GPS timestamp, per-field accuracies, originating device
capabilities.api: CMOdometerData {startDate, endDate, gpsDate: Date; speed, speedAccuracy, deltaDistance, deltaDistanceAccuracy, deltaAltitude, verticalAccuracy: CLLocationDistance/CLLocationAccuracy; slope, maxAbsSlope: Double?/NSNumber? (degrees); originDevice: CMOdometerOriginDevice .local/.remote/.unknown}
capabilities.permission: unknown — no producing API is documented
capabilities.minIOS: 17.0 for the measurement fields (class annotated iOS 8.0 / watchOS 1.0; originDevice, slope, maxAbsSlope from iOS 15.4)
capabilities.notes: ORPHANED TYPE — see blockers. Announced on Apple's Core Motion updates page (June 2023): 'Use the CMOdometerData class to get odometer data from workouts, such as speed, slope, distances, and altitude.' But NO public API in CoreMotion returns it. Exhaustion performed: (1) the complete framework symbol index at /tutorials/data/index/coremotion; (2) every topicSection across 532 crawled CoreMotion doc JSON pages; (3) the full references graph — only the framework landing page links it; (4) the xamarin-macios coremotion.cs bindings — interface present, no delivering class; (5) the WWDC23 session 10179 transcript — not mentioned; (6) HealthKit's HKWorkoutSession header — no reference. originDevice's .local/.remote cases imply cross-device (Watch↔iPhone) workout mirroring is the intended vehicle. Unusable until Apple documents a producer.

capabilities.stream: 1 Hz heart rate with confidence (denser than HealthKit's ~5 s workout samples)
capabilities.api: CMHighFrequencyHeartRateData : CMLogItem {heartRate: Double (BPM); confidence: CMHighFrequencyHeartRateDataConfidence .low/.medium/.high/.highest; date: Date?}
capabilities.permission: unknown — no producing API is documented
capabilities.minIOS: 17.0 (watchOS 10.0) — watch-sourced by implication, but no producer exists to confirm
capabilities.resolution: 1 Hz per Apple's own class abstract: 'A class that represents heart rate data collected at 1 Hz'
capabilities.notes: SAME ORPHANED-TYPE PROBLEM as CMOdometerData — announced in Core Motion updates June 2023 ('Use the CMHighFrequencyHeartRateData class to get heart rate data, including the confidence level') with no public producer found by the same six-way exhaustion check. It inherits CMLogItem, so it carries both a boot-relative timestamp AND its own wall-clock date. If a producer surfaces this is strictly better than HealthKit for HRV-adjacent work.

capabilities.stream: Step counts (LEGACY path)
capabilities.api: CMStepCounter.queryStepCount(from:to:to:withHandler:) / startStepCountingUpdates(to:updateOn:withHandler:) / stopStepCountingUpdates() / isStepCountingAvailable()
capabilities.resolution: Steps only — no distance, floors, pace, or cadence
capabilities.notes: DEPRECATED — flagged deprecated on iOS, iPadOS, Mac Catalyst and visionOS in Apple's current doc data. Use CMPedometer. Listed only for completeness of the enumeration; it still links and runs but adds nothing CMPedometer lacks.

capabilities.stream: Ambient pressure + ambient temperature (recorded/historical form)
capabilities.api: CMRecordedPressureData {identifier: UInt64; startDate: Date} and CMAmbientPressureData {pressure: Measurement<UnitPressure>; temperature: Measurement<UnitTemperature>}
capabilities.entitlement: REQUIRED AND APPLE-APPROVED — com.apple.developer.sensorkit.reader.allow. Apple: 'the system CLOSES YOUR APP if its code signature lacks this entitlement.' Granted only for a preapproved research study. HARD BLOCKER on a free Apple ID.
capabilities.minIOS: 12.0 for the CoreMotion types; SensorKit path iOS 14.0
capabilities.backfill: SensorKit holds data ~24 h before an app may read it, then retains it for a longer window
capabilities.notes: Apple redirects CMRecordedPressureData explicitly: 'Use SensorKit's ambientPressure sensor to read ambient pressure data.' There is NO CoreMotion API returning CMRecordedPressureData. The entitlement-free way to get barometric pressure is CMAltimeter's relative-altitude stream (CMAltitudeData.pressure, kPa). Note that CMAmbientPressureData is the only place CoreMotion exposes ambient air temperature, and it is entitlement-locked.

capabilities.stream: Severe vehicular crash detection events
capabilities.api: Crash Detection events, gated by entitlement com.apple.developer.severe-vehicular-crash-event
capabilities.entitlement: REQUIRED AND APPLE-APPROVED — com.apple.developer.severe-vehicular-crash-event ('To apply for this entitlement...'). HARD BLOCKER on a free Apple ID.
capabilities.notes: Included because it is the only other motion-derived event stream Apple gates behind an entitlement and it is easy to assume CoreMotion exposes it. It does not — CoreMotion has no crash-detection class at all. Listed so the enumeration of motion-derived streams is complete.

blockers: THERE IS NO CoreMotion BACKGROUND MODE. Verified exhaustively against Apple's authoritative table in 'Configuring background execution modes': the complete iOS UIBackgroundModes list is audio, location, voip, external-accessory, bluetooth-central, bluetooth-peripheral, fetch, remote-notification, processing, nearby-interaction, push-to-talk. No motion, no fitness, no sensors. The widely-repeated forum advice to 'enable the Motion & Fitness background mode in Xcode Capabilities' (Apple forum thread 715100) is FACTUALLY WRONG — that toggle does not exist. To keep CMMotionManager or CMHeadphoneMotionManager streaming while backgrounded you must already be alive for another reason: UIBackgroundModes 'location' with CLLocationManager.allowsBackgroundLocationUpdates = true (which costs a location permission prompt and GPS battery you don't otherwise need), or 'audio' with real audio playing. On watchOS the equivalents are WKBackgroundModes 'workout-processing' and 'underwater-depth'. Source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode/configuring-background-execution-modes

BACKGROUND MOTION DELIVERY IS CONTESTED EVEN WITH A VALID BACKGROUND MODE. Apple forum thread 88480 (Sep 2017): 'Since iOS 11, on iPhone 7 Plus, we don't get CMMotionManager updates anymore when in background. This used to work well with iOS 10 and lower and still works with iOS 11 on the iPhone 6 Plus' — with UIBackgroundModes already set to audio AND location. Forum thread 126045 (iOS 13.1): CMDeviceMotion updates stop on backgrounding and require re-initialisation, with 'background location mode... seems not a sufficient setting'; that thread received ZERO replies. THE WORKAROUND the 88480 poster confirmed works: call stopDeviceMotionUpdates() then startDeviceMotionUpdates(...) again from your applicationDidEnterBackground / scenePhase handler. Neither thread has an Apple engineer reply and Apple has never documented the behavior either way. Design for it: always restart motion updates on the foreground→background transition and verify with an on-device soak test, never the Simulator.

FALL DETECTION IS ENTITLEMENT-LOCKED AND UNREACHABLE ON A FREE APPLE ID. CMFallDetectionManager requires com.apple.developer.health.fall-detection, granted only by Apple application review. A free Personal Team cannot provision it. Free fallback: HealthKit's numberOfTimesFallen quantity type (no special entitlement) — but it drops falls the user dismissed and lags the event.

THE MOVEMENT DISORDER API IS ENTITLEMENT-LOCKED AND UNREACHABLE ON A FREE APPLE ID. CMMovementDisorderManager — and therefore CMTremorResult and CMDyskineticSymptomResult — requires an Apple-granted entitlement plus contractual obligations: a mandatory first-launch disclosure screen with Apple-specified verbatim text, and a requirement to collect only from clinically-diagnosed or self-reported patients. No free-tier path exists. Tremor also cannot be well approximated from CMMotionManager: Apple's algorithm targets the 3–7 Hz resting band on a wrist-worn device and returns calibrated per-minute severity distributions; naive FFT on raw accelerometer will not reproduce it.

WATER SUBMERSION REQUIRES AN ENTITLEMENT, AND THE 6 m KEY IS NOT THE 40 m KEY. Shallow (6 m) = com.apple.developer.submerged-shallow-depth-and-pressure, added via the Xcode 'Shallow Depth and Pressure' capability. Full (40 m) = com.apple.developer.submerged-depth-and-pressure, by Apple approval only. Developers repeatedly try the non-'shallow' key for a 6 m app and hit provisioning errors (forum threads 735296, 740083). Without a valid entitlement the delegate receives CMErrorNotEntitled and NO data. Also Apple Watch Ultra (and Series 10) only — waterSubmersionAvailable is false everywhere else, including the Simulator.

SENSORKIT — THE ONLY OTHER RAW-SENSOR RECALL PATH — IS RESEARCH-STUDY-GATED. com.apple.developer.sensorkit.reader.allow is granted only after Apple approves a submitted research study, and Apple states the system CLOSES an app whose code signature lacks it. That closes off SensorKit's ambientPressure, accelerometer, rotationRate, pedometer, wristTemperature, deviceUsage and ambientLight readers for a personal project. CMSensorRecorder is the entitlement-free substitute and the reason it matters so much here.

CMBatchedSensorManager REQUIRES AN ACTIVE HKWorkoutSession. Per Apple's WWDC23 session 10179: 'this is a workout-centric API, you need to have an active HealthKit workout session to get data', corroborated by developer usage in forum thread 733858 (HKWorkoutSession created before batched updates; CMErrorDomain code 109 otherwise). Practical consequences for passive lifelogging: the Watch shows a running workout in its UI, the workout writes an HKWorkout sample into Health, and battery drain is severe. You cannot get 800 Hz silently in the background. Apple Watch Series 8 / Ultra and later only.

CMOdometerData AND CMHighFrequencyHeartRateData HAVE NO PUBLIC PRODUCER. Both are announced on Apple's Core Motion updates page (June 2023) as things you 'use... to get' data, both have fully documented property sets, and neither is returned by any API in CoreMotion. Exhaustion performed before asserting this: the complete framework symbol index at /tutorials/data/index/coremotion; every topicSection across 532 crawled CoreMotion documentation JSON pages; the full references graph (only the framework landing page links them); the xamarin-macios coremotion.cs bindings (interfaces present, no delivering class); the WWDC23 'What's new in Core Motion' transcript (not mentioned); and HealthKit's HKWorkoutSession header. If Apple ships a producer it will most likely be through workout mirroring — CMOdometerOriginDevice's .local/.remote cases point that way.

FREE APPLE ID = 7-DAY APP LIFETIME. A Personal Team provisioning profile expires 7 days after creation; the installed app then refuses to launch until you rebuild and redeploy from Xcode. For a continuous quantified-self logger this is the binding practical constraint, not any API limit — you will re-sideload weekly, indefinitely. Personal Teams are also capped at 3 registered App IDs (10 per week). The silver lining specific to THIS domain: none of the entitlement-free CoreMotion APIs above are on the Personal-Team restricted list, so pedometer, motion activity, raw IMU, altimeter, sensor recorder and headphone motion all work on a free account. Design storage so a 7-day gap in app liveness is survivable — which the 7-day pedometer/activity backfill and 3-day sensor-recorder recall happen to cover almost exactly.

CMHeadphoneMotionManager HAS NO SUPPORTED BACKGROUND PATH AND NO RATE CONTROL. Unlike CMMotionManager it exposes no updateInterval property at all, so the ~25 Hz figure is empirical and not adjustable. Apple documents no background behavior for it, and the community 'Motion & Fitness background mode' advice is invalid. Assume AirPods head-orientation logging works only while your app is frontmost.

AirPods WORN/REMOVED IS NOT AN API. CoreMotion exposes CONNECTION state only — headphoneMotionManagerDidConnect/DidDisconnect, and CMHeadphoneActivityManager.Status .connected/.disconnected. In-ear detection is not surfaced to third-party apps by CoreMotion or any other public framework. Anything built on it is an inference from CMDeviceMotion.sensorLocation flipping or from audio-route changes.

ABSOLUTE ALTITUDE IS iPhone 12 / Apple Watch 6 or SE AND LATER ONLY, AND ITS ACCURACY IS DISPUTED. Beyond the hardware gate, Apple forum thread 751610 documents absolute altitude degrading from iOS 17.4.1 onward to 'exactly the same as the GPS altitude', with barometric fusion apparently dropped, plus devices becoming persistently uncalibrated after long indoor periods. No Apple engineer response exists. Relative altitude — and especially the raw CMAltitudeData.pressure field — is the more trustworthy stream.
nonObvious: YOU DO NOT NEED BACKGROUND EXECUTION FOR THE TWO MOST USEFUL STREAMS — AND THIS IS THE WHOLE ARCHITECTURE. The motion coprocessor accumulates step/floor/distance data and motion-activity classifications continuously, whether or not your app has ever run. On next launch, CMPedometer.queryPedometerData(from:to:) and CMMotionActivityManager.queryActivityStarting(from:to:to:) recover the FULL PRIOR 7 DAYS — both documented by Apple in those methods' own discussion text. Combined with CMSensorRecorder's 3-day 50 Hz raw-accelerometer recall (also captured while your app is suspended or terminated), a personal QS app that launches once every couple of days loses NOTHING of the historical record and burns zero background battery. Almost every tutorial gets this backwards and reaches for background modes first.

CMLogItem.timestamp IS SECONDS SINCE BOOT, NOT WALL-CLOCK. Every CMAccelerometerData, CMGyroData, CMMagnetometerData, CMDeviceMotion and CMHighFrequencyHeartRateData carries it, and it silently resets to ~0 on every reboot. Convert with Date(timeIntervalSinceNow: sample.timestamp - ProcessInfo.processInfo.systemUptime), capture that offset ONCE per app session, and persist it alongside the samples. Compute it lazily at write time instead and a reboot mid-session shifts an entire block of your archive by the uptime delta — with nothing in the data looking wrong.

RAW IMU NEEDS NO PERMISSION PROMPT; STEP COUNTS DO. CMMotionManager's accelerometer, gyroscope, magnetometer, and full deviceMotion (attitude, gravity, userAcceleration, rotationRate, calibrated magnetic field) deliver with NO runtime authorization and no Motion & Fitness toggle. The moment you touch CMPedometer, CMMotionActivityManager, CMAltimeter, CMSensorRecorder, CMHeadphoneMotionManager or CMMovementDisorderManager, NSMotionUsageDescription becomes mandatory and its absence CRASHES the app (Apple's word, not a warning). Practical consequence: a denied Motion & Fitness permission does NOT disable raw motion logging — you can still derive steps yourself from userAcceleration.

CMSensorRecorder IS THE ONLY ENTITLEMENT-FREE WAY TO GET RAW ACCELEROMETER DATA FROM A PERIOD WHEN YOUR APP WASN'T RUNNING. 50 Hz, recorded even if the app is suspended or terminated, retained 3 days, no entitlement, works on a free Apple ID. Nothing else in the domain does this — SensorKit does it better but is research-study gated. Undocumented gotchas that make people give up: (a) up to 3 minutes of delivery lag before new samples appear; (b) accelerometerData(from:to:) rejects spans longer than 12 hours, so a 3-day pull needs six-plus paged queries; (c) it silently records nothing until Motion & Fitness has been granted, and the only way to trigger the prompt is to CALL recordAccelerometer(forDuration: 0.1) — there is no requestAuthorization method; (d) isAccelerometerRecordingAvailable() is reported false on pre-A10 devices (iPhone SE 1st gen, 6s) and true from iPhone XR, a gate Apple has never documented.

THE HEAD-POSE ENTITLEMENT IS A RED HERRING FOR MOTION. com.apple.developer.coremotion.head-pose is named as though it gates CMHeadphoneMotionManager. It does not. Its documented effect is exclusively spatial-AUDIO orientation: AVAudioEnvironmentNode.isListenerHeadTrackingEnabled, AudioToolbox's kAudioUnitProperty_SpatialMixerEnableHeadTracking, and PHASEListener.automaticHeadTrackingFlags. Reading AirPods attitude/rotationRate/userAcceleration needs only NSMotionUsageDescription. Anyone who reads the entitlement name and concludes AirPods head tracking is gated will abandon a capability that is actually free.

currentPace AND currentCadence EXIST ONLY ON LIVE UPDATES — THEY ARE PERMANENTLY nil IN THE 7-DAY BACKFILL. averageActivePace is the sole pace-family field that survives a historical query. So if pace or cadence matters to your model, that is the one and only reason to keep a live CMPedometer session running; everything else you can harvest retroactively. Correspondingly, CMPedometerEvent (walk-bout pause/resume) has NO historical query at all — there is no queryPedometerEvents — so precise walk-bout boundaries are lost forever unless you were live.

CMAltitudeData.pressure IS THE HIDDEN CROSS-SESSION SIGNAL. relativeAltitude is zeroed at the first sample of every session and is therefore worthless across app restarts — but the sibling `pressure` field in the same object is absolute barometric pressure in kPa, fully comparable across sessions, reboots and devices. Log pressure, not relativeAltitude, and derive altitude yourself. It also needs no iPhone-12-class hardware, unlike CMAbsoluteAltitudeData. Bonus: on Apple Watch Ultra, CMWaterSubmersionMeasurement.surfacePressure delivers a second independent barometric stream even when the watch is completely dry.

CMMotionActivity's SIX FLAGS ARE NOT MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE AND CAN ALL BE FALSE. Apple's own example: a car stopped at a red light reports automotive == true AND stationary == true. And 'it's also possible for all of the properties to be set to false when the device is in motion but the movement doesn't correlate to walking, running, cycling, or automotive travel.' Any classifier written as a switch over one activity type will silently mislabel a large fraction of a real day. Store the full 6-bit vector plus confidence, never a single collapsed label.

CREATE EXACTLY ONE CMMotionManager FOR THE WHOLE APP. Apple: 'Create only one CMMotionManager object for your app. Multiple instances of this class can affect the RATE at which the system receives data from the accelerometer and gyroscope.' Two managers do not fail loudly — they quietly degrade each other's sampling. This bites hard in SwiftUI, where it is natural to instantiate one per view.

THE ATTITUDE REFERENCE FRAME YOU PICK DETERMINES WHETHER heading EXISTS AT ALL. With .xArbitraryZVertical or .xArbitraryCorrectedZVertical, CMDeviceMotion.heading returns a NEGATIVE number as an in-band 'invalid' sentinel rather than nil or an error. You must start device motion with .xMagneticNorthZVertical or .xTrueNorthZVertical to get a real heading — and true north additionally depends on CoreLocation having a fix, failing with CMErrorTrueNorthNotAvailable otherwise. Always gate on availableAttitudeReferenceFrames() first, and note the north-referenced frames run the magnetometer and cost meaningfully more battery.

CORE MOTION HAS BEEN FROZEN SINCE SEPTEMBER 2024 — iOS 26 ADDED NOTHING. Apple's own 'Core Motion updates' page has no entry after September 2024 (Apple Watch Series 10 shallow-depth support). Nothing was added for iOS 26. iOS 27 — public beta 2 as of 22 July 2026, developer beta 4 as of 20 July, shipping September 2026 — adds exactly four symbols, all currently undocumented by Apple: CMRecordedDeviceMotion, the CMBodyIdentifiable protocol, CMMotionManager.deviceMotionBody, and CMDeviceMotion.headingAccuracy. If you are planning around 'what's new in motion', the answer for iOS 26 is literally nothing, and for iOS 27 it is a possible offline device-motion recording path worth tracking through the betas.

CMHeadphoneActivityManager (iOS 18) CLASSIFIES THE PERSON, NOT THE PHONE. It returns the same CMMotionActivity payload as CMMotionActivityManager but derives it from AirPods motion, so it keeps working when the phone is on a desk or in a bag in another room. For a QS app this fills the single biggest gap in phone-based activity tracking. Caveat: unlike its phone-based sibling it has NO historical query, so it is live-only.

CMFallDetectionEvent CAN BE DELIVERED MORE THAN ONCE FOR THE SAME FALL. Apple: 'your app may receive the same event multiple times, for example, if the app crashes and relaunches.' The documented dedupe key is the event's .date, which Apple guarantees is unique per event. Any naive append-on-callback logger will double-count falls after any crash.

SUBMERSION DEPTH DATA ARRIVES AT 3 Hz WHILE SUBMERGED AND SLOWS OR STOPS AT THE SURFACE. Apple: 'The system sends measurement updates three times a second while the watch is submerged. When the watch is on the surface, the system provides updates at a slower rate, and may stop providing updates if the watch isn't moving.' A dive logger that treats a gap in updates as a session end will truncate every surface interval.

THE 'underwater-depth' WKBackgroundMode CONFERS 30 MINUTES OF FRONTMOST TIME JUST BY EXISTING. Apple: 'Unlike most extended runtime sessions, your app doesn't need to START an extended runtime session to gain additional time as the frontmost app. Just by adding this key, the system automatically keeps your app as the frontmost app for 30 minutes after the wearer launches it.' It also enrols your app in the system's autolaunch-on-submersion list. That is the longest guaranteed frontmost window Apple grants any watchOS app.

APPLE'S DOCS ARE JAVASCRIPT-RENDERED, BUT EVERY PAGE HAS A JSON TWIN. https://developer.apple.com/tutorials/data/<doc-path>.json returns the full structured page — abstract, discussion, declarations, topic sections, and crucially metadata.platforms[] with introducedAt / deprecated / deprecatedAt / beta flags per platform. https://developer.apple.com/tutorials/data/index/<framework> returns the complete symbol tree with [BETA] and [DEPRECATED] markers. This is how the iOS 27 additions above were found and how 'CMSensorRecorder is not deprecated' was PROVEN rather than assumed — the flags are machine-readable and the rendered HTML hides them.
